title: India trumpets $4.6 billion of investment in home-grown components - Telecoms
body: The Indian government has approved a series of projects that will collectively plough 418.64 billion rupees, or US$4.6 billion, into the manufacture of electronic components under a scheme designed to further the ongoing Made in India initiative. Specifically, the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) has given the green light to 22 proposals submitted to its Electronics Components Manufacturing Scheme (ECMS) last year. "The ECMS seeks to integrate India’s electronic industry with global value chains by encouraging production of essential components, sub-assemblies, and raw materials within the country.". "These approvals will significantly strengthen domestic supply chains, reduce import dependence for critical electronic components, and support the growth of high-value manufacturing capabilities in India," the statement reads. "These approvals under the Electronics Component Manufacturing Scheme reflects a bold, forward-looking step in electronics manufacturing journey, which is closely aligned with the Prime Minister Narendra Modi's vision of making India a global hub for electronics manufacturing," it concludes.

title: How Global Semiconductor Supply Chains Are Reshaping Electronics Manufacturing - Global Trade Magazine
body:
The semiconductor industry’s growing strategic importance has encouraged governments and private companies to invest in domestic and regional manufacturing capabilities. New fabrication facilities, research centres, and packaging operations are being developed to strengthen production capacity and reduce dependence on limited manufacturing locations. [...] As a result, semiconductor manufacturing has developed into a highly interconnected international industry. Changes in trade policies, geopolitical conditions, production capacity, and transportation networks are shaping how electronics manufacturers source components and organize operations. These developments are reshaping traditional manufacturing strategies and making supply chain management an increasingly important business priority.

## The Growing Complexity of Semiconductor Production [...] International trade policies and geopolitical tensions are influencing where semiconductor companies invest and manufacture their products. Governments increasingly recognize chips as strategically important resources because they support economic activity, technological development, communication infrastructure, and national security.
